reply:
INT(11) holds 10 digits max, not 11. The 32-bit signed range is –2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647. The (11) is display width for ZEROFILL only; it does not restrict storage.

Your first answer was correct—a 12-digit number overflows INT. But the reason is the 32-bit limit, not the parentheses. BIGINT (64-bit) goes to about 9.2 quintillion, 19 digits, so it handles 12 digits.
